numbered_claims.excerpt: § Lemma 9 (composition). If η is a morphism of set-systems from S to S 1 , and η 1 is a morphism of set-systems from S 1 to S 2 , then η 1 ˝ η is a morphism of set-systems from S to S 2 . If η and η 1 are locally surjective (resp. foldings), then η 1 ˝ η is also locally surjective (resp. a folding).

numbered_claims.excerpt: § Lemma 14 (pullbacks). Let S, S 1 , T be Σ-set-systems, and η : S T , η1 : S 1 T be morphisms. There exist a Σ-set-system P and morphisms π : P S and π 1 : P S1 such that η ˝ π “ η 1 ˝ π 1 , and P is universal with this property, i.e., for all Σ-set-systems U and morphisms τ : U S and τ 1 : U S 1 , if η ˝ τ “ η 1 ˝ τ 1 , then there exists a unique morphism θ : U P such that τ “ π ˝ θ and τ 1 “ π 1 ˝ θ.

numbered_claims.excerpt: § Lemma 15 (pullbacks of systems). Let S, S 1 , T be Σ-systems, let η : S T and η 1 : S 1 T be morphisms, and let P be their pullback constructed in Lemma 14. The restriction Preach of P to the vertices reachable from its unique initial vertex is a system, that folds to S and S 1 via the restrictions of the foldings from P . Thus, the pullback property is still valid when restricted to systems.
numbered_claims.note: Pullback in the category of fully supported systems, including unique factorization.

numbered_claims.excerpt: § Lemma 102 (regular branches). Let B “ pH, Σ, ∆, Ωq be an unfold-automaton. A run ρ on a representative system S is accepting if and only if ρpπq P Ω for every regular branch π of S. Consequently, B accepts a closed regular-tree r if and only if there are a representative S P r and a run on S such that all regular branches are accepting.
numbered_claims.note: All finite and infinite branch conditions checked through regular branches.

unnumbered_obligations.name: Effective MSO-to-mu translation
unnumbered_obligations.note: A total executable compiler enumerates bounded Boolean modal tables and tests finite reachable graph codes. Syntax-computed algebra, profile, Safra, parity and small-model bounds prove correctness under finite bisimulation invariance. The finite proposition vocabulary is explicitly encoded.
